Use the model above to calculate the value of $2÷\frac{3}{5}.$
question.worked_solution:
To calculate $2÷\frac{3}{5}$, we first need to divide each of the $2$ wholes into $5$ equal parts.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144806/assets/18252aca223fa7861bd1c55b53514853bb0ecb5584742ad6f6c127b71791188d.png)

 

Next, we break this into groups of $3$:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144806/assets/18af0e24ce19e818f9b3ec3189db0e4edecbf06789667dbe3cfa97173ba69996.png)

 

Note the following: 

- We got $\boxed{\text{3}}$ full groups.

- There is $1$ piece left over out of a possible group of $3.$ So the fractional part of our answer is 

$$
\frac{1}{3}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
2÷\frac{3}{5}=\boxed{\text{3}}\,\frac{1}{3}.
$$
